raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With many decode requests running, their reserved decode headroom can drive `PrefillBudget.remaining_total` negative. `available_chunk_tokens` then falls back to the full `chunk_limit` so an in-progress chunked request can make progress, but it never checks that those tokens are free. The scheduler then crashes in `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend`:

```
RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size.
Try to allocate 16384 tokens.
Available full tokens: 3200 (full_available_size=3200 + full_evictable_size_=0)
```

## Modifications

- `PrefillBudget.available_chunk_tokens` returns `None` when the budget is exhausted, so the continuation parks until running decodes free their headroom. This matches `SWAPrefillBudget`.
- The fallback dates from #12333, when an unadmitted chunked request leaked memory. The scheduler now handles a parked chunk: it skips the stash when the chunk computed no new KV, which hybrid-SWA already relies on. A parked chunk cannot starve, since new requests are not admitted while the budget is negative, and decodes finish or are retracted.
- Added a regression test to `test_prefill_adder.py`. It fails on `main` (the chunk is admitted) and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: scheduler admission only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

@erikwijmans nice one, we hit the same line from a different side, so +1 from us. no decode headroom in our case, its a P/D prefill engine (no running batch at all), the pool just had nothing left when the next chunk came.

Kimi-K3 P/D prefill, TP8 / EP8, 8 x B300, HiCache host tier + Mooncake L3, `--schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first` (#40024, thanks @Oasis-Git, our short prompt ttft p90 went 37 s -> 9 s with it), chunked prefill 16K and 32K. agentic trace replay at 24 sessions, prefill crashed 2 of 2 runs (after 18.5 and 21.8 min), all 8 ranks:

```
RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size.
Try to allocate 14272 tokens.
Available full tokens: 0 (full_available_size=0 + full_evictable_size_=0)
```

14272 = 16384 - 33 pages, thats the continuation alone after `shortest_prefill_chunk_limit` capped it, forced in by the `else chunk_limit` fallback in `available_chunk_tokens`. spf puts short requests next to the running chunk, n on our trace those bring 100K+ cached tokens each back from the host tier, so the pool fills in a pass or two. with `lpm` the chunk mostly runs alone so we never saw it there.

checked ur change, same steps on both sides:

| | main [3c56008](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/3c560089e1818a5217a73f2168273485a5350341) | main + this PR ([54ca150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/54ca1509d8077ed1025b11169646c3dd07447405)) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unit test below: spf continuation, 0 free, 0 evictable, no running batch | fails: a 14336-token chunk is admitted | passes: the chunk waits, the short request gets `NO_TOKEN` |
| `test_prefill_adder.py`, `test_schedule_policy.py`, `test_prefill_memory_budget.py` | 80 passed, 1 failed (the new test) | 82 passed |
| one B300, Qwen3-0.6B shapes, HiCache + spf, repro below, 3 seeds x 5 rounds of 17 requests | server dies in round 0 on all 3 seeds | all 85 requests served on all 3 seeds |
| Kimi-K3 v0.5.22, one node (aggregated), same scheduler flags, only this line switched | all 8 ranks down in the first round | 51 of 51 requests served over 3 rounds |

<details><summary>unit test (test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py)</summary>

```python
    def test_shortest_prefill_continuation_waits_for_free_kv(self):
        """A prefill engine with no running batch can have every KV slot held by
        admitted requests. A capped continuation must then wait instead of
        taking a chunk the allocator cannot serve."""
        adder = self.create_shortest_prefill_adder(chunk_tokens=16384)
        policy = SchedulePolicy(
            policy="shortest-prefill-first",
            tree_cache=RadixCache.create_simulated(),
            enable_hierarchical_cache=True,
            enable_priority_scheduling=False,
            schedule_low_priority_values_first=False,
        )
        continuation = self.create_shared_req("continuation")
        continuation.full_untruncated_fill_ids = list(range(200_000))
        continuation.prefix_len = 64 * 1024
        short = self.create_shared_req("short-with-host-hit")
        short.origin_input_ids = list(range(150_000))
        short.full_untruncated_fill_ids = short.origin_input_ids
        short.num_matched_prefix_tokens = 148_000
        short.host_hit_length = 148_000
        short.best_match_node = short.last_node
        short.needs_host_load_back.return_value = True
        # No free and no evictable KV: the pool holds admitted requests only.
        self.mock_token_allocator.available_size.return_value = 0
        adder.chunked_req_limit = policy.shortest_prefill_chunk_limit(
            continuation, [short], adder.rem_chunk_tokens, adder.page_size
        )
        self.assertEqual(adder.chunked_req_limit, 14336)

        self.assertIs(adder.add_chunked_req(continuation), continuation)
        self.assertEqual(adder.can_run_list, [])
        self.assertIsNone(continuation.extend_end)
        self.assertEqual(
            adder.add_one_req(short, has_chunked_req=True, truncation_align_size=None),
            AddReqResult.NO_TOKEN,
        )
        self.mock_tree_cache.init_load_back.assert_not_called()
        self.assertEqual(adder.can_run_list, [])
```
feel free to take it into this PR if useful.
</details>

<details><summary>one-GPU repro</summary>

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 30000 \
  --max-total-tokens 65536 --page-size 64 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --max-prefill-tokens 2048 \
  --schedule-policy shortest-prefill-first \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4 --hicache-write-policy write_through \
  --max-running-requests 64 --context-length 40960 --disable-cuda-graph
python3 spf_chunk_oom_client.py http://127.0.0.1:30000 0
```

(we ran it with the Qwen3-0.6B config, `--load-format dummy --skip-tokenizer-init`; weights dont matter here, the client sends token ids.)

```python
import random, sys, time, concurrent.futures as cf
import requests

URL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://127.0.0.1:30000"
SEED = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0
rng = random.Random(SEED)
ids = lambda n: [rng.randrange(100, 30000) for _ in range(n)]


def gen(input_ids, max_new):
    r = requests.post(f"{URL}/generate", timeout=600, json={
        "input_ids": input_ids,
        "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": max_new, "temperature": 0, "ignore_eos": True}})
    r.raise_for_status()


docs = [ids(6000) for _ in range(24)]  # 144K tokens: most end up only in the host tier
for d in docs:
    gen(d, 1)

for rnd in range(5):
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(17) as ex:
        futs = [ex.submit(gen, ids(38000), 8)]  # long prompt, chunked
        time.sleep(0.02)
        # short requests: a host-cached 6K prefix + 128 new tokens each
        futs += [ex.submit(gen, docs[i] + ids(128), 64) for i in range(16)]
        errors = sum(f.exception() is not None for f in futs)
    alive = requests.get(f"{URL}/health", timeout=5).ok if errors == 0 else False
    print(f"round {rnd}: {17 - errors}/17 ok, server healthy: {alive}", flush=True)
    if not alive:
        sys.exit(1)
```
</details>
